sections.history: Thirukkadaiyur, a town in Mayiladuthurai district not far from the coast at Tharangambadi, is one of the eight Ashta Veerattanams and among the best loved of them, for it remembers Shiva's victory over Yama, the lord of death. The Tevaram saints sang the Lord here, and it is a Paadal Petra Sthalam of the Chola country. Its inscriptions are rich: a record of Rajaraja I's thirteenth regnal year notes a merchant's endowment of paddy, one of Rajendra Chola's time provides for an annual eight-day festival, and one of 1054 under Rajadhiraja gives land to feed seventeen devotees. Under Kulothunga I the brick walls were rebuilt in stone and the front mandapa raised. The temple is administered today by the Dharmapuram Adheenam.
sections.architecture: The temple spreads over broad courtyards in the Dravidian manner, entered through a towered gateway, with the sanctum of Amritaghateswarar and a separate, much-visited shrine of the goddess Abirami. Its great treasure is the bronze of Kala Samhara Murthy — Shiva striding out, his foot raised against the fallen Yama — which is carried out on festival days. The stone walls and the front mandapa recall the Chola rebuilding under Kulothunga I.
sections.legends: The boy-sage Markandeya, granted to his parents on condition that he would live only sixteen years, spent his short life in devotion to Shiva. When the day came, he clung to the lingam here, and Yama's noose fell around both boy and lingam. Shiva burst forth, struck down Yama and made Markandeya forever sixteen — the Lord as Kala Samhara, conqueror of death. Centuries later the devotee Abhirami Bhattar, lost in contemplation of the goddess, named a new-moon day as the full moon; tradition says she cast her earring into the sky to make the moon shine, and he sang the Abhirami Anthadhi.
sections.festivals: Couples come throughout the year to mark their sixtieth, seventieth and eightieth birthdays — Shashtiabdapoorthi, Bhimaratha Shanti and Sathabhishekam — with prayers for long life before the Lord who conquered death. The festival of Kala Samhara, Thai Amavasai in memory of Abhirami Bhattar, Navaratri for the goddess and Maha Shivaratri are the great days; confirm dates locally.
sections.experience: Thirukkadaiyur is alive with family celebration: elderly couples garlanded and seated for their rites, grandchildren crowding the halls, the nagaswaram sounding in the courtyards. Among them, pilgrims of the Veerattanam circuit come to stand before the bronze of Kala Samhara, and many sing a verse of the Abhirami Anthadhi at the goddess's shrine.

visit.timings: Open daily in morning and evening sessions with a midday closure; auspicious days for the long-life ceremonies are very crowded. Confirm current timings locally before visiting.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional dress is expected — shoulders and knees covered; footwear is left outside before entering. Follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.photography: Photography is not permitted inside the sanctum; in the outer corridors, ask the temple staff before taking pictures, especially of rituals and the festival bronzes.
visit.gettingThere: Thirukkadaiyur lies on the Mayiladuthurai–Tharangambadi road, about 20 km east of Mayiladuthurai and a few kilometres from the coast. Mayiladuthurai is the nearest major railhead; Tiruchirappalli is the nearest large airport, with Puducherry also reachable by road.
